title: Remote Sensing B 2027: Observable Earth
summary: Twenty-five to thirty-five percent of the score is remote sensing concepts; the rest is interpreting real imagery from a list of platforms the rules close. The manual permits five equations and allows only three of them to be tested with numbers.
objectives: Apply the wave equation, Wien's law and the radar range equation quantitatively, and the others qualitatively
Choose between passive and active sensing for a stated observation, and interpret radar backscatter
Match an orbit class to a mission purpose and explain the four resolutions and their trade-offs
Name the sensor, bands and resolution of every platform on the permitted list
Read marginal information, then measure distance, area, elevation and slope from an image or map
Detect and explain vegetation change, surface temperature, elevation change, geohazards and land cover change

units.title: Properties of Light
units.summary: Everything a passive sensor records is light that met something. Five equations are permitted; three may be tested with numbers.
objectives: Use the wave equation and Wien's law quantitatively
Explain scattering, absorption and reflection qualitatively

lessons.title: The Electromagnetic Spectrum
lessons.objective: Order the spectral regions by wavelength and energy, and name the regions remote sensing uses: UV, visible, NIR, SWIR and thermal IR.

lessons.title: c = λν
lessons.objective: Compute wavelength from frequency or frequency from wavelength using the speed of light, with units.

lessons.title: Wien's Displacement Law
lessons.objective: Compute the wavelength of peak emission from an object's temperature, and use it to say which band senses a given surface.

lessons.title: The Stefan-Boltzmann Law and Emissivity
lessons.objective: State how emitted power depends on temperature and explain emissivity, qualitatively.

lessons.title: Reflection, Refraction and Snell's Law
lessons.objective: Describe specular and diffuse reflection and state Snell's law qualitatively as light passes between media.

lessons.title: Scattering, Absorption and Why the Sky Limits the Sensor
lessons.objective: Distinguish Rayleigh from Mie scattering by particle size and wavelength, and explain how aerosols degrade collected data.

lessons.title: Irradiance, Radiance and the Inverse Square Law
lessons.objective: Distinguish irradiance from radiance and apply the inverse square law qualitatively to a source at increasing distance.

lessons.title: Polarization
lessons.objective: Describe what polarized light is and give a remote sensing situation where polarization carries information.

units.title: Passive and Active Sensors
units.summary: What the rules permit: optical and thermal passive sensing, and radar as backscatter, SAR, InSAR and altimetry.
objectives: Choose a sensor type for a stated observation
Compute a radar altimetry range

lessons.title: Passive: Recording Light That Was Already There
lessons.objective: Explain what a passive sensor measures in the UV, visible, NIR, SWIR and thermal IR, and state what it cannot do at night or through cloud.

lessons.title: Active: Sending the Signal Yourself
lessons.objective: Explain what an active sensor transmits and measures, and why radar works at night and through cloud.

lessons.title: Backscatter and What Makes a Surface Bright
lessons.objective: Explain how surface roughness, moisture and geometry set radar backscatter, and interpret a bright and a dark area on a radar image.

lessons.title: SAR and InSAR
lessons.objective: Explain what synthetic aperture achieves and what InSAR measures, at the interpretive level the rules allow.

lessons.title: Radar Altimetry and the Range Equation
lessons.objective: Compute range from a two-way travel time and the speed of light, and say what altimetry measures over ocean and ice.

lessons.title: Digital Elevation Models
lessons.objective: Explain how a DEM is produced from radar and what elevation, slope and contour products come from it.

lessons.title: The Instrument Types the Rules Name
lessons.objective: Match scanning systems, multispectral imagers, radiometers, thermal imagers, radar altimeters and SAR instruments to what each produces.

units.title: Orbits and Why a Satellite Is Where It Is
units.summary: Six orbit classes, one equation. The orbit decides revisit time and coverage.
objectives: Match an orbit class to a mission purpose
Apply Kepler's third law qualitatively

lessons.title: LEO, MEO, HEO and What Each Is For
lessons.objective: Distinguish low, medium and high Earth orbit by altitude, and state what each is used for in Earth observation.

lessons.title: Polar and Non-Polar Orbits
lessons.objective: Explain why a polar or sun-synchronous orbit gives global coverage at a consistent local time, and what that buys an imaging mission.

lessons.title: Geostationary and Geosynchronous
lessons.objective: Distinguish geostationary from geosynchronous, state the altitude, and explain why GOES sits there.

lessons.title: Kepler's Third Law
lessons.objective: Relate orbital period to orbital radius qualitatively, and predict how period changes when altitude does.

units.title: The Four Resolutions
units.summary: Spatial, temporal, radiometric and spectral. Missions trade them against each other and the trade is examinable.
objectives: Say which resolution a stated task needs
Explain a trade-off between two of them

lessons.title: Spatial Resolution and Pixel Size
lessons.objective: State what spatial resolution means, and decide whether a given feature can be resolved at a stated pixel size.

lessons.title: Temporal Resolution and Revisit Time
lessons.objective: Explain revisit time and say what temporal resolution a change-detection task requires.

lessons.title: Spectral Resolution and Bands
lessons.objective: Explain band width and count, and say why more, narrower bands distinguish materials a broad band cannot.

lessons.title: Radiometric Resolution and Signal-to-Noise
lessons.objective: Explain radiometric resolution as sensitivity, and relate it to signal-to-noise ratio and the number of levels recorded.

lessons.title: Why You Cannot Have All Four
lessons.objective: Explain the trade-offs among the four resolutions and justify a mission's choices from its purpose.

units.title: The Platforms You May Be Asked About
units.summary: A closed list: Landsat 5-9, Sentinel-1 and 2, Terra's MODIS and ASTER, SRTM, ECOSTRESS and GOES.
objectives: Name each platform's sensor, bands and resolution
Choose the right platform for a stated observation

lessons.title: Landsat 5 to 9: TM, ETM+ and OLI
lessons.objective: Describe the Landsat series, name the TM, ETM+ and OLI instruments, and give the band set and spatial resolution of each.

lessons.title: Band Combinations and What Each Shows
lessons.objective: Choose a Landsat band combination for vegetation, water, urban or burn assessment, and say what colour each target takes.

lessons.title: Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2
lessons.objective: Distinguish Sentinel-1's radar from Sentinel-2's multispectral optical imaging, and state what each is used for.

lessons.title: Terra: MODIS and ASTER
lessons.objective: Contrast MODIS's wide swath and coarse pixels with ASTER's narrow swath and finer thermal bands, and say which suits which task.

lessons.title: SRTM, ECOSTRESS and GOES
lessons.objective: State what each of SRTM, ECOSTRESS and GOES measures and the product a question would hand you from each.

units.title: Reading Images, Maps and Marginal Information
units.summary: Most of the points. Before interpreting anything, read the margin.
objectives: Extract location, date, scale and orientation from marginal information
Measure distance, area, elevation and slope from an image or map

lessons.title: What the Margin Tells You First
lessons.objective: Read location, date, scale, orientation, legend and labels from an image or map, and say why each changes the interpretation.

lessons.title: Natural Colour, False Colour, Grayscale, Thermal, Radar
lessons.objective: Identify which display type an image uses and state what bright and dark mean in each.

lessons.title: Distance, Perimeter and Area From Scale
lessons.objective: Compute a real distance, perimeter or area from a measured length and a stated map scale, with units.

lessons.title: Contours, Elevation and Gradient
lessons.objective: Read elevation from contours, compute a gradient from rise over run, and identify steep and gentle terrain on a map.

lessons.title: Topographic Maps and Aerial Photographs
lessons.objective: Read a topographic map's symbols and compare the same ground on a map, an aerial photograph and a satellite image.

units.title: Observing and Monitoring the Earth
units.summary: Sixty-five to seventy-five percent of the points is interpretation, and this is what it is interpretation OF.
objectives: Read a change from a pair of dated images
Explain what a classification map does and does not show

lessons.title: Albedo, Reflectance and Classifying Land
lessons.objective: Use reflectance and albedo differences to classify surfaces such as water, vegetation, bare soil, snow and built-up land.

lessons.title: Vegetation and NDVI
lessons.objective: Explain why healthy vegetation is bright in the near-infrared, and interpret an NDVI image or time series.

lessons.title: Thermal Imaging and Surface Temperature
lessons.objective: Interpret a thermal image, explain the urban heat island, and say what ECOSTRESS adds.

lessons.title: Elevation Change and Subsidence
lessons.objective: Detect uplift or subsidence from repeat elevation or InSAR products and name what causes each.

lessons.title: Volcanoes, Landslides, Floods and Wildfires
lessons.objective: Identify each of these four hazards in imagery and say which sensor and band best reveals it.

lessons.title: Glaciers, Rivers and Stream Patterns
lessons.objective: Identify glacial movement and fluvial features from imagery, and read a drainage pattern.

lessons.title: Supervised and Unsupervised Classification
lessons.objective: Distinguish supervised from unsupervised classification, read a classified map, and use the NLCD change index.

lessons.title: Land Cover Change, Urbanisation and Deforestation
lessons.objective: Read a land cover change from dated images and state the human or environmental implication the rules name.
